text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Zip Wireless Activity Tracker, Magenta All it does is record the number of steps I have walked since midnight. Based on that, it guesses how many calories I have burned. Usually the time is displayed correctly. No date.

Any wrist holder for the Zip may not record steps correctly. My wife has a Fitbit Charge HR that does not record when she pushes a shopping cart.

The silicone holder or 'case' is also the clip. I keep mine in my jeans watch pocket. The clip is unnecessary for me.

The tool to open the battery door is just that, the tool to open the battery door. It serves no other purpose. It WILL be needed when the battery has to be replaced. That battery is a 3-volt button / disk cell (CR 2025).

In the year I have been using this, the Fitbit battery has been replaced 3 times. Today I had to reset the Fitbit Zip because the time was off several hours and minutes, and the number of steps should have been above 6,000 but had dropped to 360.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Zip Wireless Activity Tracker, Magenta

Universal UB300 Adjustable Bench (Discontinued) This is the perfect bench for a home gym. It has all of the incline levels I need to do my workouts. I like how it also has a -10 degree incline for situps, etc.
The material covering the bench is high quality and has held up to workouts easily. It is also easy to clean in between workouts. Changing the incline is straight-forward and due to the simplicity in the design it will hold up longer than other benches with a more complicated incline selection mechanism. One thing that is a bit annoying about this bench are the foot pegs. The round plastic side pieces that keep the pads on will pop out very easily. Any real use will pop them out and I guarantee within a week or two those plastic pieces will be lost.

Dimensions are confirmed as advertised.

Pros:
*Easy to select incline
*Durable
*Easy to clean

Cons:
*Side plastic pieces on foot pegs easily pop out(-1/2 a star)

Additional Considerations:
Make sure you purchase the proper weights and other safety equipment to go along with this bench. If you are bench pressing, get a power rack and do not bench without a spotter.

Overall: 4.5/5 stars (>=.5 rounds up, <.5 rounds down) => 5 stars

text_fidelity_a:
Harbinger Flexfit Ultra WristWrap Lifting Gloves I have owned a pair of Lee Haney lifting gloves with wrist wrap for 19 years and which I used three times per week for about 12 of those years. I still have those gloves and although they are a bit stiff, you'd never know they were used so much as they hardly look worn. Since the Lee Haney gloves are not padded, I decided to try these gloves both because I expected an increase in comfort and as an enticement to get me back into lifting again.

The gloves I received are a size "Large" and they are heavier than any other lifting gloves I've tried before; the pair weighs in at 6.2 ounces according to my dietary food scale. However, you don't notice the weight when wearing them. Below are the pros and cons I noticed during use:

PROS:

1. The gloves are well padded. In fact, the padding is an excellent feature for when I perform lifts where the weight is in the palm of my hand, such as when doing a bench press or incline press or when the weight is evenly distributed throughout the hand such as when doing squats using a [[ASIN:B0000AVAL2 Advanced Fitness Manta Ray]].

2. I usually take a size medium or large in a woman's glove and this size large fit me comfortably.

3. The extra "leather-like" flap that you secure to the fastened wrist wrap offers extra security so that the wrap won't come undone during a lift and the gloves will remain securely fastened.

CONS:

1. The padding on the pinkie finger was uncomfortable for me when doing dead lifts because the bar was evenly distributed through my hand and the padding on the pinkie finger seemed to get in the way. It almost caused a pressure point of discomfort during each entire lift (ascent and descent).

2. The wrist wrap was awkward to fasten because not only did I have to wrap the strap around my wrist, but then I had to flip over the "leather-like" flap and make sure it fastened to the Velcro on the back of the flap.

3. I was bothered by the white tag inside the right glove during lifting. Perhaps the manufacturer could either leave the tags out or put them on the non-Velcro portion of the wrist wrap.

4. I don't like that the two pieces of fabric used to fasten the glove to the cardboard insert it came with remain sewed to the glove. Basically, the gloves arrive with two tags on each glove that fastens to the cardboard packaging. Those tags remain as part of the glove and to me they are annoying as I see no reason to ever use those tags again.

I do think that if men are considering purchasing these gloves, they might want to consider ordering the next size up. My boyfriend always takes a size "Large" in men's gloves and he had to struggle to get these size Large gloves on his hands.

These gloves are thick and although they feel well-made they don't look well-made on close inspection. Therefore, I'm concerned that the stitching on the padding may come loose. When comparing these gloves to my Lee Haney gloves, I doubt they will last as long but only time will tell.

If padding is important, then these gloves offer that and certainly cushion the lifter during many lifts. However, for me I can only give these gloves an average rating because of the cons and my concern that the stitching around the padding will come loose.
text_fidelity_b: Harbinger Flexfit Ultra WristWrap Lifting Gloves

text_fidelity_a:
Jaybird Reign Advanced Active Fitness Recovery Band - Black - S/M I bought this from Amazon based on all the 5 star reviews. I have been wearing it consistently for 11 days and following the instructions as noted in the on-line user guide videos. I am torn as to whether to give this 3 or 4 start. I ended up going with 4 stars because I have tried other trackers and the REIGN feature-set is hands above the other devices I have tried. For me it is the best choice available, today.

PROS
SIZING: Band design and fit is excellent. You are given 3 band lengths with every device, which ensure you will get the perfect custom fit. Before you buy, I strongly recommend you go the the Jaybird REIGN site's FAQ pg for exact sizing info. http://www.jaybirdsport.com/static/img/reign/sizing-guide.jpg
Be aware, you want to determine the side-to-side width across the TOP of your wrist, not the circumference of your wrist. The REIGN is a 2 piece band. The fit/width of the top piece is what determines which size to buy. You then customize your fit with the bottom band, which is provided in 3 lengths.

SECURE: the magnetic locking mechanism ensures your band will never fall off. The design allows you to easily secure your band with one hand. Once it is magnetically secured, it will not come off until you manually disengage the magnets. Excellent design!

COMFORT: Due to the lightweight, smooth silicone band, this is the MOST comfortable activity wearable I have ever tried. As a tech professional, I am typing on my keyboard all day long and cannot wear any watch-type devices or jewelry on my wrists. This is the 1st tracker device I have found that I can wear all day, every day. I barely notice it's on my wrist. I wipe mine down with a damp cloth. I have had no irritation or discomfort. 5 stars!

TRACKING: The REIGN will track data by specific activity, which you will not get with other devices. It detects Walking, Swimming, Biking, Running and General activity. In addition to the 3 silicone magnetic wrist bands, they provide 2 stretch style athletic bands and an ankle biking band. The STEP tracking is accurate for me ( Compared my data for a couple of days with a FitBit and Treadmill)

SMART PHONE APP: The design of the SmartPhone app is a plus. The information provided is very good. In additional to your GoZone score, you are given 3 screens of data: Activity, Sleep and History. Each screen presents you with a Summary view and a Detail 'Timeline' view of that data.

VISUAL FEEDBACK: The band itself provides visual indication of your progress towards your GoZone Goal via lights. Each light represents 9% of your goal. (Dont bother enabling the 'Time' feature. The lights flash for 1 second and is pretty much useless)

CHARGING: Very easy to pop the device out of the band and charge on the charger that is included. Via USB cord, it can be charged thru your laptop or a plug, your choice. As stated, it takes about 3 hrs to initially charge. I pop mine onto the charger before I hop in the shower. Easy-peasy. Please note, if you lose the charger, you will have to buy a replacement since the charging doc is required.

USER GUIDE: I recommend you watch the online User Guide videos AND read thru the entire list of FAQs prior to purchasing/using the REIGN. There is a lot of info in the FAQs that is not covered in the User Guide videos that you will want to be aware of. A nice feature is, the videos are also part of the SmartPhone app.

HISTORY: the SmartPhone app. provides a History screen with Day, Week, Month & Year mode. Once you select your mode, you can then swipe thru by Day, Week, Month...... Very nice.

PERSONALIZED: The REIGN definitely does 'get to know you'. After the 1st week or so, the daily goal has adjusted, based on my history.

CONS:
GO ZONE: Upon waking up, you should be able to sync and log that day's GO ZONE feedback in 2 minutes. I have owned the REIGN for 11 days and rarely have I been ale to get GO ZONE to completed on the 1st try. Once the REIGN device is Connected to the SmartPhone app. and I Start Go Zone, I often get error messages and have to Start again. These issues are definitely specific to the GO ZONE feature, as I do not get errors throughout the day when syncing. This is the key feature of the device, so I expect it to work without issue and not have to battle with it.

SUPPORT: Unfortunately, I cannot give a good review on support. I sent a very detailed Email with screenshots from my SmartPhone listing the GoZone errors and Sleep monitoring issue I have experienced. The response I received was very friendly, however the only thing the reply told me was I could manually enter Sleep info in the app. There was no response to my detailed GoZone issues and questions.
SUPPORT Review Update 12-29-2015: I received another reply from Jaybird Support addressing my specific concerns and questions. They have provided me with instructions of how to reset my Reign pod, indicating this may resolve my specific issues.

READABILITY: I think the design of the app is great and it is easy to use. However, it is not so easy to read on your Smart Phone due to the funky color of the font (pale yellow-green) against a light grey background. It is not configurable. I understand these are the branded colors, but they do not lend themselves to readability on mobile devices.

DASHBOARD: There is not an online Dashboard. Your data is only available via your SmartPhone app. I went to the website and attempted to login assuming there would be an online dashboard. The online login is a separate account and is for purchases, only. The other tracker devices I have used have online Dashboards and settings, which I deem as a plus.

DATA SYNC: Data sync is on-demand, which preserves you SmartPhone battery (Yay!). However, for some reason, data for previous day(s) is not always shown in the app. Periodically, when you open the app on your phone, it will show all zero's after syncing. I have not been able to detect a pattern. It is an intermittent issue that cannot be reproduced, on demand. The work-a-round is to close and reopen the app.

TACTILE: Tapping the REIGN device 4 times does not active my lights. I have to rap it pretty hard, 8 to 12 times. I have mine set for progress feedback, only. The lights flash for 1 second. I would prefer a button that will allow me to quickly turn on the progress lights and turn them off when I release the button. ( If there were a manual button, the 'Time' feature may be of value).
text_fidelity_b: Jaybird Reign Advanced Active Fitness Recovery Band - Black - S/M

SCHWINN Crewmaster Rower 100660, Gray We have a Schwinn recumbent bike that's held up well over the years, so were excited to try a Schwinn rower. This arrived well-packed in a series of boxes (be prepared to have a lot of packing materials to deal with), and it took about an hour to unpack and assemble, at least with two people. There's two main pieces that are heavy, and everything is included to put it together (other than something sharp to cut up the boxes, ties and packaging. There's a metal bar you need to remove from the front to put the 'stabilizer' in place, probably to keep anything from bending while in transit.
The motion is smooth once everything is together and the resistance is adjustable, which is good because you'll be able to use the equipment for a while.
You definitely need a pair of shoes while working out because of the position of the screws, and the screen/monitor is a little on the cheap side (it's powered by batteries and doesn't have a lot of options other than keeping track of your workout).
The long 'track' bar can bend upward to 'save' space or allow the machine to be moved about, but it still takes up a good bit of space and is heavy, so I don't think everyone will be able to move this about. But it is a good rowing machine and it does provide a great workout.

text_fidelity_a:
Zefal 164 Water Bottle, 33 oz I do like having these bottles for bikepacking. It makes the difference between having to carry some kind of bladder vs making the jump between towns in the middle of summer during midday. The 1L capacity is the big appeal for me.

For me, the Camelback Podium water bottles are the best I've used. I would rate the Podium at 4 stars. I've gotten used to the annoyances and now I have really on positive associations with that water bottle .

This Zefal bottle gets additional points for capacity, and loses many points for the following criteria:
Distinct plastic taste that appears very quickly. With my other water bottles, I detect some leeching only when I leave water in the bottle overnight or longer. With the Zefal, it's almost immediate. That worries me.

Requires too much force to seal the lid. On my first bikepacking trip with these, I kept wasting water because my first squeeze after each stop would go on my face and jersey, in addition to my mouth. I'm used to it now and I know how hard I need to muscle on the lids.

No jet nozzle. This is the same basic design as water bottles had 40 years ago. It's not horrible - it works like it's supposed to; OTOH if the Camelback is 4 stars then this design is worth much less.

Branding: I simply feel strange about branding on really low-end items. IDK - maybe I'm afraid that people with think that I think this is great water bottle? Maybe I shouldn't take that out on the product. I definitely don't mind the Camelback logo, no matter how outlandish and counter to my design taste, and yet with these bottles even the conservative branding seems to be in bad taste.

Overall, this bottle simply fails to meet my criterion for good cycling gear: its interface/use is not transparent. I.e. instead of simply using it routinely / out of habit / on muscle memory, I'm always aware of opening the valve, tasting plastic, and remembering to close the valve as I return it to the cage. Gear that I consider over the threshold for good sinks down out of sight much faster than my habit formation with these - assuming I will ever get used to them. At this point it seems more likely that next summer I'll set out of find a better solution to this same problem.

I simply don't like these bottles.

Overall this feels like many levels of quality down from the Camelback bottles. I find the capacity appealing and really nothing else. It's like the quip about cookie-cutter, drywall box "McMansion": it's not home, but it's much.
text_fidelity_b: Zefal 164 Water Bottle, 33 oz

VELAZZIO Polarized Sunglasses for Men Women Fashion Sunglasses UV400 Protection Lightweight Good basic inexpensive sunglasses that block uv400 and are polarized. However, there are reviews on here saying these are a “high quality product.” These are good quality for the price point. But for this price obviously the frame is plastic, lenses are basic triacetate & can scratch easily, polarization film is on the outside of the lens which can degrade and are not very impact resistant.
Compare that to higher quality sunglasses (typically above $100) the lens material is likely to be polycarbonate. The polarized film is sandwiched between two layers of polycarbonate meaning the polarized film can never wear out and provides impact protection. That’s the big difference.
I like these glasses for just a basic pair to use for activities where I’m afraid to use my nicer sunglasses. Are these worth the price? Yes I believe these are a good value, have great looks and provide the basics. However, there are others out there for half this price that can provide the same basics but sometimes lack in style and fit.
I would say the glasses are a bit narrow on my face but I like the look and was surprised these were nicer than expected.
text_fidelity_b: VELAZZIO Polarized Sunglasses for Men Women Fashion Sunglasses UV400 Protection Lightweight

TOMALL Replacement Clip Holder for Fitbit Alta/Fitbit Alta HR I bought one of these right after I bought my Alta because I read a review here from Paula titled "Almost like having a One". I loved my One, wore it daily for years till it finally disappeared, and by then Fitbit had stopped making it. Shame, too, because I'd have bought a new one.

I don't care for wrist fitness trackers - they tend to count arm motions, and besides, I don't even wear a watch.

So while my Alta doesn't do everything my One did - the display is small to fit the format, so after a thousand steps, it shows you 1.5K rather than say 1,552 steps, and it also doesn't track stairs and stair equivalents. But honestly I'm pretty happy. I can wear my Fitbit on my waist, which is how I always wore my One.

The TOMALL Replacement Clip Holder for Fitbit Alta/Fitbit Alta HR isn't irritating to my skin, it clips firmly on my pants without creating a hole, and it fits the Alta really well, with a little hole at either end to fit the parts of the Alta that usually fit on the band. The shoulder straps are padded well enough for my light duty needs, but I don't know that I would want to carry this pack fully loaded for several days. I do like the pocket on the waist area for quick access to keys and my phone though.

There's enough room inside for a change of clothes, extra shoes, the rubber shoes for the dogs, dog water bowl, snacks for me and the dogs, extra flexi leash, basic first aid kit, water bottles for me and the dogs, my pistol, flashlight, emergency survival kit, a map and compass. When we hike, it's typically in the deep West Texas deserts of Big Bend, Terlingua and the Chinati mountains along the Rio Grande at the ranch. We don't camp out there deliberately, but you must always be prepared for whatever the Chihuahuan Desert throws at you.

My one star deduction is because this pack isn't really water resistant like it claims. A single, light shower and everything was slightly damp. Not wet, but heading that way. The reason mostly is because there's a ventilation hole on the top center on the back and it might as well be open. There is an included rain cover sheet thing so it's not a total loss, but still....don't carry this if you think you'll be out in inclement weather.

Discraft 160 Gram Sky Styler Sport Disc I really like this disc for throw and catch frisbee in light to know winds. Mostly I throw a 175G Innova Pulsar. But in no wind to light breezes this think is a blast to throw. I throw frisbee with a partner a couple of days a week and I've been throwing on and off since, cough-cough, the 80's.

This disc will do more in a light wind than the 175g Ultimate discs. Meaning you can curve it, it will drift a bit on the wind, catch an updraft and float, etc. It's also great for throwing it as hard as you can since it's lighter and easier to catch. It's also a great disc for warming up before getting out a heavier disc. You wouldn't think 15G would make much of a difference but you definitly feel the difference when throwing a catching.

I don't know if it's a thing for freestyle, but it has no thumb grooves on top. After a couple of throws I stopped even noticing it didn't have them.

It's just a really good all around disc for throw and catch frisbee if you don't need the the weight of a 175g disc.all the time. If I could only have one disc, it would be the 175g Pulsar but since I can have more than one disc, this would be the 2nd disc if I could only have 2.

Also for a beginning thrower, who wants something to toss around at a picnic, with the kids in the backyard this is the better choice than the heavier 175g discs. For young kids while I haven't thrown it you might want to consider the even lighter J-Star. from Discraft.
text_fidelity_b: Discraft 160 Gram Sky Styler Sport Disc

text_fidelity_a: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) I have been wanting a Fitbit for a really long time.  I did some research because I was not sure which one I wanted.  I went to the website and read about them all.  This one had all the features that I wanted.  I never wear a watch and my cell phone is too big to fit in my pocket while I work out.  So it was important for me that I could view time with my Fitbit.  Just a tap of the screen and I can view the time.  Or I can just flick my wrist and the time displays.  Or I can press the button on the side.  The Fitbit HR is thicker than what I would have liked, but it is not worth giving it less than 5 stars over that.  I can view my steps and check my heart rate.  Many reviews have said that the heart rate is not accurate.  Honestly that is not a feature that was a make it or break it to me.  I don't know if the heart rate is accurate or not.  The Fitbit also lets me know how many miles I have walked. It also tracks if I went up any flights of steps or not. I can even use it as an alarm.  It just vibrates gently.  Setting up the Fitbit and syncing it to my Android phone was a breeze.  The app is great.  The Fitbit HR also tracks my sleep patterns.  I can set challenges for myself and even challenge others.  The first day I set up a challenge to take 10,000 steps.  Throughout the day whenever I am near my phone with my Fitbit on, they sync and update.  I got special badges for being close to my goal.  It really encouraged me to make sure that I got to my 10,000 steps.  With the app I can log how much water I have drank and how many calories I have eaten and how many I have left.  My husband loves my Fitbit HR and really wants one for himself.  The directions say not to take a shower or go swimming in it.  That is perfectly fine with me.  I just take it off when I take a shower.  I am glad that I went ahead and purchase my Fitbit HR.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in))

text_fidelity_a:
Sig Sauer BUCKMASTERS Scope- 3-12x44MM BDC It's been a while now, but products coming out of China are starting to rival top quality manufacturing elsewhere. This scope is a clear sign of that. The coating is smooth with no blemishes, the glass is properly and evenly multi-coated, the reticle is straight, and knobs give you decent feedback on the turns, and the flaps have tastefully relieved SIG logo on the inside (so when you flip them open EVERYONE can see what you working with [as if it matters] but still cool). The throw lever had some blemishes on it and wasn’t screwed all the way in. The Box it comes in is very simplistic – a good thing – with minimal packaging and waste. Even the handkerchief is a nice quality and small, not like grandma’s undies that sometimes come with other scopes. I also dig on the reticle shape which reminds me of an orthodox cross – it’s not too thin or thick, just the way you’d like it (is what she said, yeah, I know…). Also, looking inside the scope with super high lumen light reveals, dare I say, precision – something unexpected at this cost level. I think Sig’s trying to introduce these in the best light possible so as to grab market share. Well, their marketing is your win (for now at least)
But wait, what’s that thing on the side, looks like scribbles or some kind – what IS that?! Meatballs with wafting smell coming off them? Frog eyes? Female crocodile cartoon eyes peeking just above the surface of the water… Let me get closer… Nah, it’s a STAG! With tiny little red beady eyes. And deformed horns. WHO thought of this logo?! Watsamadderwidu?! It’s possible the weirdest logo I’ve ever come across – it’s like slapping flame prints on a Bentley. Iiiish…
But then again, who cars, the paint doesn’t drive the car. So with that little minus, I’d say Sig’s again a winner. BTW, remember the old Nikon Buckmaster scopes? They were totally awesome maaaaaan… But then Nikon got out of the biz, so I’m wondering if there’s any connection between Sig’s Buckmasters and the Nikon Buckmaster series. Whatever the case, I highly recommend this scope. (and if you don’t like the logo, put tape over it!)
text_fidelity_b: Sig Sauer BUCKMASTERS Scope- 3-12x44MM BDC

Colisal Trekking Poles Collapsible Hiking Sticks for Women Men Walking Sticks Lightweight with EVA Foam Grip and Paired with Rubber Tips and Snow Basket Trekking Sticks 1 Pair 125cm I purchased a pair of trekking poles over 15 years ago and paid a lot of money for them. Although I do not use them a lot, I always had trouble with them, particularly getting on the snow/mud basket.

Therefore, when these became available, I wanted to see how they stacked up. These are not heavy duty like the expensive ones but they are still impressive, especially at the $31.99 price point.

They come collapsed as seen in the first photo. I did have some difficulty understanding how to get these to lock in place when fully assembled.  I had to pull down on the top of the pole until the little nub shown in photos three and four popped out. It sort of locks into place like an umbrella locks with the nub.

Once the pole is assembled, which is really quick to do once I figured out how to lock it, then it has to be adjusted to height. The clasps above the nub (photos three and four) opens to  relieve the tension on the telescoping pole in order to make the height adjustments.

All that is left to do is to cinch the wrist strap with enough room to hold on to the poles yet also allow one to release them. The strap locks into place with a plastic piece in the handle once the desired wrist width is reached.

I have no plans to collapse these poles again but that can be done if necessary. I got these for  my boyfriend and he loves them. He walked with them already. He just has to get use to using poles on a hike or walk.

Note that these poles come with a mud basket that can be screwed on (photo five) or it can be used without (photo six).

For the price, these are a good, lightweight alternative to the expensive ones and they are collapsible which makes them more portable than the other poles.
text_fidelity_b: Colisal Trekking Poles Collapsible Hiking Sticks for Women Men Walking Sticks Lightweight with EVA Foam Grip and Paired with Rubber Tips and Snow Basket Trekking Sticks 1 Pair 125cm

text_fidelity_a:
Thule Apex XT Bike Hitch Rack We are so impressed with this bike rack. It's nicer than any other that we have seen. It includes tools to help with assembly, but my husband chose to use his own adjustable wrench and socket set. It comes in 2 main pieces. You put those pieces together before installing it on your vehicle. There's a pin that is used to connect the 2 pieces. It did give my husband a little trouble at first when trying to push the pin in, but then he noticed that it was more like a bolt and threaded, so he used his socket set and screwed it in and that worked very well.

The next issue we had was putting the rack onto the receiver. There's a knob on the base of the rack that you tighten to lock it in to the receiver. You have to use the key to engage the knob in order to get it to work. At first, we didn't figure that out and it was hard to get it into the receiver and back out. In hindsight, it makes a lot of sense. Without the key, it can't be removed from the car so it can't be stolen. The instructions showed the key and knob, but there were only pictures, so we didn't really understand what it was getting at. Some verbal instructions would have helped with that.

Once the rack is installed, it doesn't budge. It's very sturdy and extremely well designed. We have a Toyota Sienna and you can swing the rack (with bikes) completely out of the way so you can open the trunk. That's a pretty cool feature! There are plenty of straps included to secure the bikes in place. The manual didn't show how to hang a women's bike, so we had to look online to figure out how to do that. There's also a cable lock that prevents the bikes from being removed from the rack without the key. That wasn't something we figured out right away either. That's another item where an explanation would have been helpful.

Overall, we are very happy with this. It is nicer than we expected and we highly recommend this.
text_fidelity_b: Thule Apex XT Bike Hitch Rack

text_fidelity_a:
Gaiam Pilates Total Toning Kit NOTE: I received a free copy of this workout kit to review for the web site Metapsychology Online Reviews.

Ana Cabán has been a mainstay of Pilates media for almost a decade now, but she is constantly adding new and varied challenges to her workouts. Here she includes 2-lb. hand weights fashioned into a unique "S" shape to increase the intensity of the program. The DVD offers three different 15-minute workouts, each of which incorporates the weights and yet are still based on the traditional exercises first introduced by Pilates founder, Joseph Pilates. Cabán works out alone in an outdoor setting; her purple mat is featured on a raised platform against a mountainous background. The music is generally pleasant and unobtrusive.

The Main Menu of the DVD offers options to select the Introduction, Mat Series, Equipment Series, or Standing Series. If you choose to start with the Mat Series as Cabán recommends, you can easily continue to complete the entire 54 minute workout, as there is only a brief pause between each section. In Mat Series (15 mins.), Cabán first uses the weights to move the arms from over the head to down towards her sides. Still holding the weights, Cabán does the Pilates Hundred move, keeping the weights still at her sides rather than pumping the arms as is customary. She continues with a classical Pilates matwork sequencing of movements, sometimes holding just one weight--for example, she performs Rolling Like a Ball holding one weight with both hands in front of the calves. All five exercises of the Series of Five are performed, using both weights for the first three exercises and just one weight for the last two. Cabán concludes the Mat Series in a seated position for the Spine Stretch forward (holding one weight behind the head) and the Spinal Twist (holding one weight straight out in front of the body).

The Equipment Series (19.5 mins.) is also performed entirely on the mat. Cabán begins with one weight in each hand for a move called Coordination and then continues on to the Rowing series, a sequence of several different classic Pilates exercises. Other exercises performed seated include Shaving the Head and Hugging a Tree. Still holding both weights, Cabán then moves to a prone (face-down) position for the Long Box series, which involves reaching the arms up and back as well as up and out to the sides. Next are several movements completed while on the back or seated, including a Back Stroke (again coordinating the movements of the arms and legs), a Teaser variation (holding the Teaser position while pumping the arms with the weights; repeat several times), and Short Box variations. After a brief side stretch, Cabán comes to a kneeling position, still using both weights for Chest Expansion, Thigh Stretch, Arm Circles, Bicep Curls, and Rolling In and Out. Cabán concludes this segment with the Mermaid, incorporating one weight at a time to increase the stretch.

The final segment is the Standing Series (19.5 mins.). Here Cabán beings in a standing position for Running in Place and Rolling through the Feet, adding in arm movements (holding both weights) to each of these exercises. These moves serve to pre-fatigue the upper body for a traditional series of Pilates arms work, including Bicep Curls, Tricep Extensions, Zip Ups, The Bug, Little Circles, and Boxing. For many of these exercises, Cabán begins with the heels grounded but then rises onto the toes as she repeats the exercise. She continues to hold both weights for all of the remaining moves, which include Lunges, Side Bend, "Hide Your Hands," Pick a Flower, Wall series, Arm Lifts, Arm Circles, and finally, Roll-Downs.

Overall, I was very impressed with this workout kit. The design of the S-weights seemed very ergonomic in nature, as they were extremely comfortable to use, offered even distribution of the weight, and were very easily incorporated into the flow of the workouts. Given this, I actually felt the exercises more intensely than I ever have before. I consider myself to be an a perennial intermediate level in Pilates; although I have always enjoyed Pilates matwork, I have never gotten much out of the other Pilates exercises--e.g., the Rowing series, the Pilates Arms work, etc.--in the past. But Cabán's distinctive method of putting these movements together along with the S-weights truly made a difference.

Cabán does not mirror-cue, but she has an excellent, easygoing instruction style; she does assume some pre-existing familiarity with basic Pilates moves here. In summary, I would highly recommend this workout set, particularly for intermediate level and above Pilates practitioners.
text_fidelity_b: Gaiam Pilates Total Toning Kit

text_fidelity_a:
ACCUSPLIT AX740 PRO MEMORY (50) DUAL LINE STOPWATCH I often have three or 4 different workout groups going on at the same time and I have two of the older model 740MX watches and two of the newest AX740's to help me manage it all. What I like best about this watch is that after hitting the split button which I do at the beginning of every repeat in a set, I can hit the release button and the watch will show BOTH the Total Running Time AND the running repeat time. So if I am running a set of 100's on 1:20 I hit the split button at every 1:20, then hit the release button, it shows me the running repeat time so that I can eyeball the splits during the repeat and I can shout out times as they are coming in. It also shows the number of repeats so that I never lose count of the number of repeats. So with multiple groups and multiple watches it really helps me stay organized and allows me to give better feedback to the swimmers. I have had the two 740MX's for 10 years now and have used them nearly every day and often twice a day. Recently one or the other will blank out occassionally so I have purchased the newer AX740. I am not mentioning the blanking out as a problem but more of a testament that they have lasted this long under heavy use.

These are also wonderful watches for swim meets especially when you have the luxury of one watch per swimmer. Hit the split, write it down (or let the memory save it for later), hit release and see the total running time as well as the split running time.

If there is one drawback to this watch, it's that reset is made by holding down the start button for 2 seconds -- which seems like forever when you are trying to run a bunch of individuals doing one at a time 25's and you want to get ready for the next swimmer NOW. The older versions had a similar reset but it was about 1.3 seconds, the newer AX740 is a full 2 seconds. Sometimes I think my older watches are beginning to fail because I hold down the split button as hard as I can wishfulling thinking that it will speed up the reset. A light touch does the same and may lead to a longer life of the watch.
text_fidelity_b: ACCUSPLIT AX740 PRO MEMORY (50) DUAL LINE STOPWATCH

text_fidelity_a:
Compaclite Patented Oversize 360 Swivel Steel Camping Portable Chair for Outdoor Camping / Picnic / Hiking / Bicycling / Fishing / BBQ / Beach / Patio with Carry Bag, Lime Green I have two versions of the Compaclite chair: the 360 swivel version as well as the high back version with a pillow. There are substantial price differences. This swivel version retails for about $60 while the high back is roughly half the price at $34. They both have the same level of comfort (which is passable) and take the same amount of time to assemble (a few minutes to set up and break down). I ultimately would recommend the cheaper version as, clearly, it is half the price and offers the exact same things, unless being able to turn around in circles is a priority for you.

I do enjoy the fact that this can be broken down and stored in a bag. Although it takes more time to put together than your typical camping chair, it’s worth it for it to be compact. Getting the corners of the chair into the poles isn’t incredibly difficult, but it does take some elbow grease; I assume this will become easier with time. I do think having the drink pocket on the front of the chair is a design flaw and the sides of the chair actually come up a bit high to be comfortable for your arms. It's QUITE quiet. The only real noise is the friction of the runners at the base, unavoidable. Watching TV or listening to music easily drowns it out. The beeps mentioned by others IS also annoying. It's loud for no good reason. After the warranty is up, I might look into opening it up and putting something to adjust the level. I ran for a little over an hour today with my wife sitting only ~6 feet away watching TV and it didn't bother her at all.

I'm 5'9" and the height is fine. My setup isn't - best place to use is under a build (down) ceiling covering heating ducts, so it's pretty low. If I'm not careful, I bump my forehead. The fan blows more on my chest than neck or face.

I'm currently not in the greatest shape, but I generally use it at the 4th or 5th intensity level and move at the 6.8 (mph?) pace. I've used it 4 times for a total of about 4:30 hrs. My shoes were tight, so once I took them off. Bad idea. The treads were not good on my feet; the soles are still sore.

It fits in a small space much better than I expected. It can easily set almost right up next to a wall, unless you need access from either side.

I don't imagine I'll test out the speakers much, as if I'm running inside, I'll likely watch TV shows or movies, or do as I do when I run outdoors, listen to music with earbuds.

After a couple uses I noticed that I could hear a jingling sound. I remembered to check it after today's session and the bolt/nut on the front right tread was loosening. Glad I caught it. I tightened it up and will keep an eye on it.

So far I'm quite happy with choosing this elliptical. If I had the extra $200, I might have gone with the next model up, but I have no regrets on this purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Horizon Fitness EX-59 Elliptical Trainer

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Versa Special Edition Smart Watch, Charcoal Woven, One Size (S & L Bands Included) Battery
I’ve had this watch for about a year and the battery life has gone from a week to about 24 hours. The advertised quick text replies didn’t work on any platform for months after the watch came out, and after having the watch for a year they eventually reported that they would never work with the iPhone (this was not reported prior to the release).

Period tracking
The menstrual cycle tracking is not remotely accurate. For the first few months after it came out it seemed like it was just predicting The same date(s) each month (which was not that far off and not all that unhelpful) but at some point it got off and trying to change it didn’t work and it’s never been even close again.

Data entry
After the most recent software update it was supposed to be possible to (finally) enter exercise and water directly on the watch but it does not work. It’s possible to enter the information and looks like it is saving, but it does not actually transfer to the dashboard, and when I check back on the watch later the data is gone.

Sleep
The sleep tracking accuracy is harder to determine. It does not seem to match with how I feel, but the hours in bed are correct about half the time. This is not so bad actually because I get up multiple times during the night and am extremely restless, which I would expect to throw off any wearable sleep tracker. A battery life that allows for sleep tracking was one reason I was interested in getting this in the first place, but it is not accurate enough to be helpful.

Heart rate
The heart rate tracking is actually pretty accurate as long as I wear the watch tight enough over the pulse point on my wrist. It also creates a graph of heart rate trends that are accurate. This has been the most accurate and helpful feature of the watch.

Dashboard
The dashboard is not at all user friendly. It is hard to enter information, and I have to use the website to enter my workouts since the automatic tracking, app entering, and watch entering do not work. Entering calories is so glitchy and time consuming it is not worth doing. After the last update I have to log into the dashboard every single time whether or not I select the option to keep me logged in.

Step counting
I can’t say exactly how accurate the step counting is, but it seems like it is pretty close. Days I walk more it’s higher, and the times I have walked on a treadmill and can watch the steps go up as I walk it seems to match closely.

Apps
This is one of the worst and most disappointing parts of this “smart watch.” NONE of the apps work, and they often cause my phone to freeze. Apps that I installed before realizing that they would not work will randomly appear back on the watch sometimes for no reason. Storing music on the watch is a complicated process that is not worth it, and playing music with it requires a subscription to Deezer which does not work as well as Apple Music and when I had it crashed all the time.

No other device I have ever crashes or causes any problems. After my experience with this watch and the lower price point on the new apple watches I am never purchasing another Fitbit product and strongly suggest avoiding them.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Versa Special Edition Smart Watch, Charcoal Woven, One Size (S & L Bands Included)

text_fidelity_a:
KastKing Sharky Spinning Fishing Reel Ultra Light Weight Freshwater Professional Open Face Reel With Features Found Only On Top Quality Penn Shimano Daiwa and Okuma Spinning Fishing Reels I love to go freshwater fishing and this weekend I approached the lake with a brand new weapon - a KastKing Sharky 6000 spinning reel. This is a serious reel that made a good day of fishing even better.

I will start by saying that even though it is approximately the same weight as my primary reel - a KastKing Orcas 4000 - it is significantly larger. I spooled on over 200 yards of 10-lb. test fluorocarbon line and it still had room for more line on it. I put it on an 8' limber rod and headed out to a productive spot.

I am very fussy about my reels and I expect them to meet several criteria. I want a good cast range, a smooth cast, smooth retrieve, quiet operation and a zero-reverse clutch. There has to be enough clearance between my knuckles and the bail to keep it from rapping me on the knuckles when I retrieve. And finally, the drag has to work and be easy to set. The Sharky met every one of these requirements.

I learned fast (and the hard way) that the reel is more than accommodating when it comes to casting and more than once I sent my lures into the trees instead of to the edge of the bank when I was unable to hit the bank with other reels on identical rods. This required a little adjustment on my part but it meant I did not have to work as hard and it also meant I could hit farther targets when I wanted to. So, when I fish from the bank I have a better range into whatever water I am fishing.

The retrieve is glassy smooth and very fast too. Not once did I have a problem with snarled line on the retrieve when I had near-zero load which is a problem on some reels. I like that I could bring in the line very quickly when needed (like for grabbing the net to assist another fisherman). The reel is quiet when spinning - not silent, but quiet.

When the ant-reverse clutch is engaged there is no reverse at all. To me this is a sign that the reel is quality made and is assembled well. I really, really dislike reels that do not have a zero-reverse clutch, and even worse is a reel that has one but it still has just a little play in it. The Sharky’s zero-reverse is solid and works exactly like it’s supposed to work - absolutely zero reverse.

The bail spins an inch or so away from my knuckles but never once has it hit my hand when spinning.

The drag set is uniform and smooth and does not really get harder to turn until close to the end of the tightening range.

In appearance this is a very attractive reel, black and red with a little bit of chrome. It is surprisingly lightweight for the size. I have bigger hands than average so a reel this size that doesn’t add much more weight is very welcome.

The reel helped me land a good variety of fish including largemouth bass, crappie and a near-citation yellow perch. The most exciting catch was a largemouth bass which was not huge but not small either and provided the best test of the reel under stress, and the reel brought this fish to the boat easily without incident. Even under the load of a fighting bass the reel was just as smooth in operation as when retrieving a test plug.

I am very, very pleased with the Sharky 6000 and will be using it again in the same lake in a few weeks. It has not let me down even once and it works very well. If you want a larger reel that works great and does not add a lot of weight to your gear, take a very close look at this reel.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: KastKing Sharky Spinning Fishing Reel Ultra Light Weight Freshwater Professional Open Face Reel With Features Found Only On Top Quality Penn Shimano Daiwa and Okuma Spinning Fishing Reels

text_fidelity_a:
Puoyis Walk Traction Ice Snow Cleats Crampons for Shoes Boots, Shoes Spikes Anti Slip Traction Grips for Winter Hiking Fishing Walking Climbing Jogging Mountaineering FIRST for those saying oh, try YAKTRAX...I DID! They did NOTHING on ice, I don't deal with snow, I deal with black ice and they DID NOT keep me from slipping. It even says in their directions about not using just on ice.

EDIT:
I have just had my second pair for a little over a month, but they started leaving RUST stains within a week.
THEY DO keep me from slipping as I take my dog out, the trash, etc., HOWEVER, while last year's pair rusted, this year, I notice they have already started leaving rust spots on my BRAND NEW large foyer mat.

THAT TICKED ME OFF, it's brand new and after winter I will have to replace because it now has big ugly rust spots from these cleats. So these cleats are costing me WAY more than nine bucks in damage.

I also had them on my foyer ceramic tile inside the door, RUST spots, BIG rust spots where some of the ice had melted.

I didn't notice that last year. So it is NOT GOOD that they are FULL of rust so fast, still work, will get me thru the winter season, but WTH?

I now have to keep a garbage bag (OR I guess you could get the exact color mat of the rust these make) near the door to put the shoes on.

ONLY good thing about these, is yes, THEY DO keep me from falling if I walk slow on black ice.
I WOULD GLADLY pay four times more for ones like that that didn't RUST!
______________________________________________________________________________

Last winter, a friend in another state knew I was having a hard time taking my dog out (no fenced in yard) over black ice. She sent me a pair because she said one of her in-laws is a nurse and has to traverse a slick parking lot and they worked well.

After a year, these did rust out, but at this price, HAPPY to get another pair, which I just did.

If you're wondering re SIZE, I wear a ladies 8.5 and these work well. I don't know how they would work for a 5 or 10 (the women's size range the medium is supposed to fit). I would check other reviews if you are closer to those sizes, for 8-9, I think you would be happy.

And can't beat the price! THESE worked SO MUCH BETTER for me than YakTrax! THOSE did NOTHING for me on ICE. In fact, in the instructions for YakTrax, they don't recommend on just ice (at least the pair I got). On snow, they may be great, on a thin sheen of black ice, NO!

Even when my dog was slipping a bit on some black ice, and dogs have claws, I wasn't. THESE ARE LIKE SPIKES.
AS LONG AS YOU MOVE FAIRLY SLOWLY, I FIND THEM EXCELLENT!

FIVE STARS PLUS. What price can you put on safety?
text_fidelity_b: Puoyis Walk Traction Ice Snow Cleats Crampons for Shoes Boots, Shoes Spikes Anti Slip Traction Grips for Winter Hiking Fishing Walking Climbing Jogging Mountaineering

text_fidelity_a:
The Flex Belt Abdominal Muscle Toner , Black, 24"-47" Bottom line: If you're looking for a magic solution that will produce firm abs with no effort, keep on looking - this won't do that (nor will anything else!). It is, however, an effective supplement to the usual ab routines. Tha major downside is the price (both initial and on-going).

Full review: Abs are one of the most difficult body parts for me to keep toned since many of the more effective exercises, such as crunches, are difficult for me to do with any degree of intensity due to chronic back problems. This looked like an interesting way to get a low-impact targeting of my abs.

The device is in essence a TENS system. That stands for transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation, and is a technique that has been used for years by physical therapists to help alleviate pain. I was first introduced to TENS therapy when I ruptured a disk and needed a few weeks of physical therapy to help with the recovery process. You can do a search on TENS and get all the specific details but in brief it involves placing pads on your body and applying an electrical charge. I know, that sounds rather Frankenstein-ish, but it's safe (if used properly) and not at all unpleasant.

The belt has three pads that it positions on your abs when you put the belt on. You can adjust the pad position based on your waist size. The manual provides clear instructions as to how/where to place the pads. There are also some very nicely done videos on their website to help with setup and usage.

The unit has a control pad that allows you to select the program and vary the intensity. There are 10 different programs that range from 20 to 40 minutes long. There is a wide range of intensity level adjustments (0 to 150) which vary it from "can't feel it at all" to "please stop!!" I was impressed at the number of settings it offers to control the intensity of the stimulation.

I found the controller to be very easy to use, with a clear display that shows the time and intensity level.

The belt is battery powered. You charge it using the supplied AC adapter. Once charged, you do not need to be plugged into the wall outlet to use it - the battery is built into the device. There's an indicator that tells you when the battery power is low and you need to recharge (which takes a few hours). Battery life is good, with each charge lasting for several sessions.

The belt is comfortable to wear and adjusts easily. I was a bit disappointed in the build quality of the belt, however. Given the price I was expecting something that was more robust. It's OK, but it's not something that wow'ed me in terms of construction quality.

There are ongoing costs in using this in that you have to replace the pads at regular intervals (the manufacturer recommends replacement after 30 uses). The replacement pads are pricy ($15), and you'll want to factor that into the total cost of ownership. You can extend the pad life by using electrode gel (such as this: [[ASIN:B0002CA8RQ Spectra 360 Electrode Gel]]. There are many other brands of gel as well). In addition to keeping the pads usable for a longer time, the gel helps increase conductivity (it's also great to use with heart rate monitors).

So, does it work? Yes - I saw an increase in ab definition after using it. However, it comes with a BIG caveat: the belt alone won't give you perfect abs. You still need to watch your diet and do conventional exercises to keep your weight down so that the flab don't hide the abs. The belt will help fine-tune the process by targeting your abs, but the belt alone won't do squat if you're overweight, or expect it to get you into shape you while you sit on the sofa eating chips.

I'll give it 4 stars since it works well and does what it is supposed to do. The manual is clear, and the product is easy to use. The main downside (and the reason for a loss of one star) is that for the price I was expecting more sturdy-feeling components or have it include more accessories, such as the attachments that you can get to target your arms. At the very least it should include a more ample supply of pads (it comes with one set).

Pricy for what you get, but it does what it says it will do.
[the manufacturer provided the product for review]
text_fidelity_b: The Flex Belt Abdominal Muscle Toner , Black, 24"-47"

Gaiam Balance Ball Beginner Kit (Small, Purple) Your first observation might be similar to mine. The outdoor setting is calming and just gorgeous. The colors in this video are beautiful and the river creates a calm, quiet and peaceful setting for your workout.

I enjoyed the workout, but didn't realize how many muscles you needed to perch yourself atop a balance ball. You start off just rolling over the ball and then progress to some pretty tough balancing acts. There are some stretches which will stretch out your spine in new ways. I realized I'm not as flexible as I thought I was.

I'd advise watching this video at least once before proceeding because it is kinda difficult to follow the workout while attempting to focus on not hurtling towards the floor if you are not totally focused on what you are doing.

The kit includes:

Medium inflatable exercise ball (green, 26"/65cm)
Full-length workout video (35 minutes)
Air pump

The Air pump is "ok," but I found that an electric pump was much more efficient. If you use the air pump, you might want to do that "workout" the day before. The instruction scare you into worrying about inflating the ball too much, but never fear, with that pump, it might be impossible.

The medium exercise ball is "ok" but had I realized there was a larger balance ball, I'd have ordered the larger one since I'm taller. If you are 5' 9" and above, I'd say go for the blue balance ball (large size). I think weight also counts. If you are above your recommended weight (ideal weight and all that), then you might want a larger size.

On the side of the box it says:

Small Purple Balance Ball - Height 5' 0" to 5' 5" - Ball Size 22"/55cm
Medium Green Balance Ball - Height 5' 6 to 5' 11" - Ball Size 26"/65cm
Large Blue Balance Ball - Height 6' 0" to 6' 3" - Ball Size 30"/75cm

The exercise video is combination of shorter segments from three balance ball workouts. You really have to concentrate on making smooth and steady movements.

The way I found this workout to be most effective was to place the ball on top of a yoga mat. This prevents slippage of the ball on a carpet and also prevents you from getting injured because the yoga mat provides an additional level of protection from your hands and feet slipping on a carpet.

You will be doing three workouts.

Upper Body
Abs
Lower Body

There are times when you are either sitting, leaning over the ball or on your back, balancing and stretching out your spine. The hardest part of this workout is when you are on you back and you are rolling on top the ball. It is easier once you make full use of your powers of concentration.

The video is a nice introduction, but is really only an introduction. While you can get a good beginner's workout, I'd imagine it is more effective to order the three additional videos they recommend. Karen Voight also has a DVD out called BLT (Butt, Legs & Tummy) on a ball.

This workout will take you to new levels of concentration and mind-body awareness. It will work the upper body, lower body and abs. You will be strengthening, toning and conditioning smaller core muscles.

The 45 minutes includes a 5-minute warm-up to learn proper positioning.

If you enjoy this workout, look for:

BalanceBall Fitness Upper Body Workout
BalanceBall Fitness Abs Workout
BalanceBall Fitness Lower Body Workout

~The Rebecca Review
text_fidelity_b: Gaiam Balance Ball Beginner Kit (Small, Purple)

I have learned that the acceptable quality of the newer reels offered, hold up fairly well and better than those in past years at lower prices. Here on the Gulf of Mexico coast where I fish, the environment on the shore, bays and on the boat causes some problems for reels.  Corrosion can occur when you forget to rinse your reel off after each time out, in hot weather when you come home spent and you just sit your rodnreels down in the front of the garage and then you grab and open a beer, only to forget them until it is too late. My other reels have all experience my neglect and for the price this reel performs well and seems good with the neglect.  I do now try to rinse them each time though, but braid holds moisture more than mono and I used braid on this reel.  So, I hope it continues to perform. text_fidelity_a:
GUANCI Silicone Collapsible Travel Cup, Silicone Folding Camping Cup with Lids, Expandable Drinking Cup Sets, Portable, Dishwasher Safe for Outdoor Hiking Travel These cups are solid performers with a few points that stop them from being excellent, though good for their price point, Specifics

Size: these are smaller than your basic 8-10 oz cup. Suitable for little kids, but you'll be pouring several cups worth as an adult drinking from them. Their small size of course though works in their favor for saving space, which if you're throwing them in a stroller pocket or a backpack or hanging them from something this is a feature, not a bug

Stability: They are stable enough if not quite as stiff as I'd like. They don't topple or warp, but if I were pouring hot water in them, say for cocoa or tea, I'd be cautious to not fill too much. But again, want to tress they do stand up empty and full.

space: their small size means they take up next to no room when compressed, maybe an inch or so thick (about the thickness of a finger) and a small lid diameter (probably a little smaller in diameter than your travel mug lid).

ease of use: They don't compress immediately, can take a little fussing, but just a few seconds, nothing overly frustrating (and sometimes you will get it in one try). Dishwasher safe, which is nice.

My comparison to these would be Sea to Summit collapsible mugs. Those are in all ways but two superior. They are thicker, bigger, more stable, have graduated measurements, and collapse in one go every time. The ways they are not as good is they don't come with a lid (though it's possible that's changed--may want to check out) and they are more expensive. Personally I think they are worth the cost, we've been using the same set for years of camping--both backcountry and dayhiking/car camping. But if you're looking to save some money are are going to use these mostly for little kids or to bring in a stroller or the like, these are a good value--adequate for their purpose and relatively cheap
text_fidelity_b: GUANCI Silicone Collapsible Travel Cup, Silicone Folding Camping Cup with Lids, Expandable Drinking Cup Sets, Portable, Dishwasher Safe for Outdoor Hiking Travel

text_fidelity_a: SABRE Ruger Pepper Spray Gun – Police Strength – Reloadable with 10-Foot (3M) Range, 5 Bursts & Enhanced Facial Coverage Interesting personal defense weapon. Quite small. I think I'd rather have the entire thing made of orange "DON'T SHOOT ME" plastic. It appears to be one of those pepper spray tubes in a pistol format. There's a push-through button on the front of the trigger guard which acts as a safety. The handle is VERY short, as in one finger of my adult sized hands, not much to hold onto. I'm not sure I'd rely on this, but then again I don't think it's humanly possible to acquire a CCW permit in San Diego County unless you're a blood relative of the Sheriff. The instructions (printed in an excruciatingly small typeface) detail how to swap out another cartridge. Remember that this or any other personal defense weapon is intended to give you enough time and space to GET AWAY from a threat, as in run like hell while screaming your head off. An attack is not a time to be calm and restrained. My point being that you wouldn't want to think of using this to "take down" a perp, strictly to buy yourself some time and space to GET AWAY at top speed. Interesting object. Legal and offers some degree of protection. Please see the photo -- this thing is small. And lightweight.

My only problem with it, and this is a BIG problem, is that the bottom is a hard plastic that slips on wooden and laminate surfaces. This is Dangerous in many ways, and also makes it impossible to do some exercises unless you use a yoga mat underneath to hold it in place.
So that's the negative. It should have had a more rubberized bottom for safety, since many workouts happen on hard surfaces. Use a mat, and it's fine.

-adding balance to an exercise means you are not only doing the exercise you planned on doing (like pushups for example), but you are also adding core with the added benefit of increasing neurological connections between your brain and muscles, allowing you to move more efficiently and with greater strength, balance, and fluidity.
-it can be added to MANY exercises
-it is small and portable
